operator_scope: live camera, read-only. The flush probe armed twice and self-restored both times. No codec, no allocation, no write to the frame, the DNG or any setting. Two recordings of about three seconds.

camera.boot: fresh; cave reported no claims this boot, both hook sites original

question: copy-back overwrites the buffer the writer hands us. A clone shares frame[0x68] rather than getting its own allocation, so does a clone exist when the flush runs?
verdict: NO CLONE EXISTS. Reproduced on two independent runs.

the_answer.claim: no Dup2 ever ran on this frame, so nothing else holds its buffer
the_answer.argument: Dup2 increments BOTH frame[0x1110] and frame[0x1114] on the owner, and it is the only place either is incremented - established statically in ledger-frame-sharing-static-20260924.json. Both read 0 on both runs. frame[0x1C0] reads 1, so a clone was REQUESTED and none was made, which is exactly the part static reading could not settle: the two call sites of FUN_c0374ee8 differ and one is ungated.
the_answer.consequence: copy-back is not exposed to the shared-clone hazard on this path.

two_of_my_four_pass_conditions_were_wron.why_it_was_wrong: I read it as 'one holder'. It counts CLONES, so 0 is the good answer and 1 would have been the bad one. My condition was inverted.
I guessed 0 was the 'I am the owner' sentinel. It is 0xFFFFFFFF. Dup2 writes the owner's id into a CLONE's field, so a non-clone never has it set.
I assumed frame[0x68] is the buffer the writer registers. It is the ALLOCATION base; the DNG starts 0x2000 into it. See the correction below.

note_on_reinterpreting: Three of four conditions did not hold as written and I am still calling the substance a pass. The load-bearing fact is narrower than the four conditions and does not depend on them: Dup2 is the only writer of frame[0x1110] and frame[0x1114], and both are 0. Either being non-zero would have been a fail and neither was. The other two conditions were guesses about sentinel values that the measurement corrected.

structural_correction_to_yesterdays_capa.what_i_said: the allocation is exactly the stock DNG size, 3,244,544 bytes, and the 8,704-byte gap between ring slots is the allocator's granularity
structural_correction_to_yesterdays_capa.what_is_true: frame[0x128] is 0x15400 = 87,040, not the 0x13400 = 78,848 I assumed. The allocation is 87,040 + 3,165,696 = 3,252,736 = 0x31A200. The DNG the writer registers starts 0x2000 = 8,192 bytes INTO that allocation and ends exactly where it ends. The gap between ring slots is therefore 512 bytes, not 8,704.
structural_correction_to_yesterdays_capa.arithmetic_that_confirms_it: frame[0x68] + frame[0x128] = 0x53B00C00 + 0x15400 = 0x53B16000, and seg[0] + 0x13400 = 0x53B02C00 + 0x13400 = 0x53B16000. The same pixel start from two different bases. This is also what confirms flush_arg1 is the frame object and that these offsets are the right ones.
structural_correction_to_yesterdays_capa.does_not_change_the_design: The copy-back rule is file_bytes <= seg[1] and it is unchanged: we write only inside the region the writer handed us. What is corrected is a claim about what surrounds that region, not the bound. There are 8,192 bytes before seg[0] in the same allocation; nothing establishes that they are ours and copy-back does not need them.

frame_kind_is_1_not_2.claim: frame[4] reads 1 on the CinemaDNG movie path, not 2 as I inferred from FUN_c037a990's branches
frame_kind_is_1_not_2.consequence: the movie frame takes FUN_c037a990's DEFAULT branch, which is the one whose formula I analysed: frame[0x128] + round_up(payload, 512). So the allocation arithmetic stands. It also means FUN_c0397cd8 does not consult the bracketing settings, which is why frame[0x1C0] stays at its default of 1.

an_outlier_that_repeating_caught.observation: the first run reported 6,208 us, 17 times the 356-382 us measured on 2026-09-24 and again on run 2
an_outlier_that_repeating_caught.handling: n = 1 is not a measurement. The second run, with the cave cleared and the probe verified fresh, reported 382 us.
an_outlier_that_repeating_caught.plausible_cause: run 1 was the first recording after a replug and a fresh boot, so filesystem or card first-write work is a candidate. NOT established.
an_outlier_that_repeating_caught.not_concluded: 6,208 us is still 522 MB/s for 3,244,544 bytes, which no SD card sustains, so even the outlier is not a full transfer. Nothing here changes the submit-versus-transfer reading.

explicitly_not_established: that no clone exists on OTHER paths or other recording modes. Two runs, one mode, one clip each.
what the 8,192 bytes before seg[0] are for, or whether anything reads them
whether the writer's buffer is aliased at +0x40000000. C1 is read-only and does not test the alias; C2's first frame is what settles it.
the aggregation state on this boot. menu SetMediaWriteMode reads 0, but the settings slot was not read this session and the menu value is not what the CinemaDNG init consults.
anything about copy-back itself: C1 only removes one hazard from its path

camera_left_as_found.note: the cave holds the flush probe's code from the second arm; inert, hook restored, cleared by a power cycle. Two clips were recorded and left on the card.
